Fit review: strong. Build an unsupervised anomaly detection method that learns a normal-traffic baseline from unlabelled Modbus/BACnet

content.text: {"issues":[{"where":"Research Question 1 / Year 2 phase","problem":"The question asks whether the model detects injected faults, but a one-class model trained only on normal data and evaluated only against its own false-alarm rate on clean data cannot demonstrate detection ability until labelled fault events exist — this is fine, but the Year 1 milestone ('validated on traffic archives') claims validation before any fault data exists, risking the milestone being interpreted as proof of detection rather than proof of normal-baseline fit.","fix":"Reword the Year 1 milestone to 'baseline model fit and normal-traffic evaluation documented' and make explicit that detection performance (RQ1) is not assessed until the scripted fault sessions in Year 2."},{"where":"Research Question 3 / Year 3 phase","problem":"A comprehension test with 'at least five plant managers' during a single field trial on one client site assumes access to that many plant managers willing to participate, but neither the company records nor the term sheet offer or confirm this access.","fix":"Replace the fixed minimum of five with 'all available plant managers at the trial site, with a floor of two', or add a fallback of recruiting additional participants via ArmaturaSec's other consenting clients."}],"unconfirmed":[]}
